Ten comments

Bill Cheatham

A tune that’s popular at my local old-timey session (Bristol, UK).

↳ Posted by Mix O'Lydian on July 10th, 2015.

Bill Cheatham, X:2

Fiddlers are quite happy to play this in “A” as in Mix’s setting.
The setting in “G” that I’m posting is preferred by many Bluegrass 5-stringers.
(When forced, they might capo up a whole step and play in “A”)
:-) RTH

↳ Posted by BillScates on July 10th, 2015.

Bill Cheatham, X:3

Here’s a version with some nice rhythms and some slightly different note sequences to the previous versions. It’s an amalgamation of various versions I’ve heard and the basis for how I usually play it.

↳ Posted by Steve Owen on July 10th, 2015.

Gan Ainm

This was a tune that I learned many years ago (70s) from a fellow who provided basic old time fiddle lessons at a Winnipeg music centre called Homemade Music. Walter was collecting tunes and sharing tunes from the far reaches of Manitoba from Metis and old time fiddlers. He was hoping to put together an anthology of tunes that he learned in rural areas of Manitoba. After I learned Liberty, he suggested that I learn this tune…he simply called it The Liberty Follower haha. After 50 years of noodling with tune and passing it on to beginners, it would be nice to know if it had an origin and a name.
Thanks Jeff Lehman
Atikokan Ontario

↳ Posted by Jeff Lehman on February 8th, 2024.
